title: Deepest, widest view of the Small Magellanic Cloud from SMASH
caption: The Small Magellanic Cloud from the SMASH survey, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope

story: This image, part of the SMASH survey, may be the finest wide-angle view yet of the Small Magellanic Cloud, one of our Galaxy's closest companions.
Of all the galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, the two Magellanic Clouds are the biggest. They also differ from the rest in that both are still busily making new stars, and quickly.

A satellite galaxy is a smaller galaxy that orbits a larger one, held by its gravity. The rest of the Milky Way's satellites are no longer actively forming stars, which is why the two Magellanic Clouds stand out. A galaxy that is still making stars keeps a supply of gas and dust, and the young stars born from it are often hot and bright. Wide, deep surveys like this one let astronomers study huge numbers of individual stars across a whole galaxy in a single consistent set of images, which helps them piece together how and when its stars formed.

understand.summary: The Dark Energy Camera on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope observed the Small Magellanic Cloud through g, r, i and z filters, covering visible and near-infrared light. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
